reason: The summary said the word of 10.1 is spoken 'because he delights in hearing': the verse says only 'to you who take delight' (prīyamāṇāya) — the object of the delight and the causal link are the commentators' specification, which the 10.1 entry itself leaves open (Arjuna's not being sated with hearing is his own word at 10.18, now cited for it). The groups of 10.6 were given in one construal; aligned with the corrected 10.6.

'the seven great seers (maharṣi) of old, and the four, and the Manus' joined 'of old' (pūrve) to the seers, as in construal (a), while splitting 'the four' from the Manus, as in construal (b): it matched neither reading the notes record. The paraphrase now gives both groupings of 'maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavas tathā'.

'abiding in the self's own state' read the reflexive ātma- of ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ as 'the self' (the pattern DECISIONS.md asks every chunk to watch); the reflexive leaves open whose being is meant — the devotees' (the reading commentators commonly give) or the speaker's own — as the entry's notes say. Now 'abiding in their own being or in my own (ātma-bhāva-stha)'.
